newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firms vs dollar on export sales.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firms vs dollar on export sales.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was firm against the dollar on Thursday on hard currency inflows from exporters, reflecting an underlying bullish tone, commercial dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.87 against the dollar compared to 53.91 on Wednesday. On the pound, the shilling was posted at a mean of 88.59 from 87.96.
"The shilling is strengthening on basic fundamentals. There are a lot of inflows but very little demand," a dealer said.
Dealers said the shilling had edged about 20 cents in the morning trading session and was trading at 53.50/70 levels.
"Today should see a further consolidation of the shilling especially since no dollar purchases seem forthcoming from the government," one dealer said.
The money market was slightly liquid with many banks lending. Overnight rates eased to between 16 and 18 percent from 16 percent and 20 percent previously.
